result: DENV-infected cells activate pDCs through an indirect, contact-dependent mechanism that selectively induces IRF7-mediated IFN-I production without triggering NF-κB-dependent inflammatory cytokine responses (TNFα). This bifurcated response is distinct from direct TLR7 stimulation and is not due to kinetic differences or active inhibition by DENV.
evaluation: Claims C29-C39 provide converging evidence from human and mouse pDCs showing selective IFN-I/ISG induction without TNFα production in response to DENV-infected cells. The use of IFNβ pretreatment (C33) and control experiments with IMQ (C35) effectively rule out alternative explanations. The data are internally consistent across multiple experimental approaches.

result: A novel pDC:Irf7+ mouse model was generated by knocking in Irf7 under the pDC-specific Siglech promoter on an Irf3/7 double knockout background. This model restricts IRF7 expression to pDCs while preserving independent NF-κB signaling and avoiding overexpression artifacts.
evaluation: Claims C40-C48 and C121 document the generation and validation of the pDC:Irf7+ model with appropriate molecular, protein, and functional characterization. Flow cytometry (C44), bioassays (C45-C46), and cytokine measurements (C47-C48) confirm pDC-specific IRF7 expression and function. The hemizygous design preserves Siglech expression (C42), and expression levels are controlled (C121).

result: In DENV-infected pDC:Irf7+ mice, despite undetectable systemic IFN-α/β protein, early ISG induction occurs across multiple tissues at 18h post-infection. This pDC-IRF7 response induces robust ISG expression without NF-κB-dependent inflammatory transcripts, demonstrating complete segregation of these pathways.
evaluation: Claims C50-C59 demonstrate a paradox resolved by localized IFN-I signaling: undetectable systemic IFN-I (C52) yet robust ISG induction (C53-C54). The data from multiple tissues and time points, combined with segregation of ISG and NF-κB responses (C57-C58), strongly support the conclusion. The lower basal ISG levels in knockout mice (C55) are appropriately explained by prior literature.

result: pDC-restricted IRF7 signaling significantly reduces DENV viral titers and RNA levels in spleen and plasma at 42-72h post-infection compared to Irf3/7 DKO mice. This viral control depends on IFN-I/IFNAR1 signaling, as demonstrated by IFNAR blockade experiments.
evaluation: Claims C60-C63 and C69-C74 provide viral titer, RNA quantification, and antibody blockade data demonstrating pDC-mediated viral control. The IFNAR blockade experiments (C69-C70, C73) establish mechanistic dependence on type I IFN signaling. The early increase in viral levels (C62) is appropriately discussed as potentially reflecting immune cell recruitment. Statistical significance is demonstrated for key comparisons.

result: pDC-IRF7 signaling accelerates the type II IFN response in DENV infection, with Ifng and Gbp2 expression detected as early as 18h and peaking at 28h post-infection in pDC:Irf7+ mice, compared to delayed induction in Irf3/7 DKO mice. This acceleration is temporally associated with viral control.
evaluation: Claims C64-C68 and C75 document accelerated type II IFN kinetics with appropriate gene expression markers (Ifng, Gbp2) and protein measurements. The temporal correlation with viral control is demonstrated. The distinction between IFN-I-induced ISGs and IFN-II-specific markers (C65) is appropriately made with literature support. The hypothesis formulation (C68) is reasonable given the data and prior literature.

result: NK cells in the spleen are the primary source of IFNγ in DENV-infected pDC:Irf7+ mice (~12% of splenic NK cells produce IFNγ). NK cell depletion significantly increases DENV viral titers and reduces IFNγ and type II ISG responses, while not affecting type I ISG levels, establishing NK cells as downstream effectors of pDC-IRF7 signaling.
evaluation: Claims C76-C86 and C140 provide comprehensive flow cytometry, depletion studies, and molecular analyses demonstrating NK cell-mediated IFNγ production. The depletion efficiency (>80%, C83) is adequate, and the effects on viral titers (C83), IFNγ levels (C84), and ISG responses (C84-C86) are statistically significant. The tissue-specific response (C78-C79) and lack of effect on type I ISGs (C86) support the proposed pathway hierarchy.

result: CHIKV activates pDCs through the same mechanism as DENV: contact-dependent, TLR7-mediated sensing of infected cells that induces IRF7-restricted IFN-α production without NF-κB-dependent TNFα responses. This mechanism is independent of the RLR pathway (MAVS).
evaluation: Claims C87-C93 demonstrate that CHIKV shares the same pDC activation mechanism as DENV using multiple experimental approaches: transwell experiments (C89), TLR7-/- pDCs (C90), MAVS-/- pDCs (C91), and cytokine profiling (C92). The data are consistent across human and mouse systems and parallel the DENV findings, supporting the generalizability of the mechanism.

result: pDC-restricted IRF7 signaling provides complete protection from lethal CHIKV infection (100% survival in pDC:Irf7+ mice vs. rapid lethality in Irf3/7 DKO mice), with tissue-specific viral control most effective in distal sites (spleen, liver). This protection depends on IFNAR signaling, as demonstrated by antibody blockade inducing lethality.
evaluation: Claims C94-C99, C101-C103, C106, and C130 provide survival data, viral titers across tissues, and IFNAR blockade experiments demonstrating complete protection by pDC-IRF7 signaling. The 100% survival (C95) vs. lethal infection in controls (C94) is striking. The tissue-specific control (C98-C99) and IFNAR dependence (C102) are well-documented. The undetectable IFN-I despite protection (C101) parallels DENV findings and supports localized responses.

result: DENV and CHIKV infections show differential outcomes in Irf3/7 DKO mice: CHIKV is invariably lethal while DENV is controlled by 72h post-infection. This difference correlates with viral titer levels and differential sensitivity to type I vs. type II IFN signaling. pDC IFN-I responses provide intermediate viral control for DENV and complete protection for CHIKV.
evaluation: Claims C105, C129-C136, and C142 document differential outcomes between DENV and CHIKV with appropriate viral titer measurements and survival data. The correlation with viral load (C133) and differential IFNAR contribution (C134) are demonstrated. The proposed role of alternate IRF proteins (C135-C136) is appropriately speculative. The differential sensitivity to IFN types (C142) is supported by literature citations.

result: pDCs are key initiators of antiviral responses to DENV and CHIKV through IRF7-prioritized signaling that excludes NF-κB responses. Despite undetectable systemic IFN-I, pDC-IRF7 signaling induces potent antiviral responses through localized, contact-dependent IFN production that accelerates NK-mediated type II IFN responses and controls viremia while avoiding inflammatory pathology.
evaluation: Claims C107-C111, C120, C123-C124, C126-C127, C150-C151 represent the major conclusions synthesizing the experimental findings. These conclusions are well-supported by the comprehensive data from ex vivo experiments, the pDC:Irf7+ model, viral control studies, and mechanistic analyses. The concept of localized IFN responses (C110, C123-C124) explains the paradox of undetectable systemic IFN-I yet robust antiviral effects.

result: Background claims establish that type I IFN responses are critical for RNA virus control, pDCs are specialized IFN-I producers, and many viruses including DENV and CHIKV do not directly activate pDCs. Pattern recognition receptors (cytoplasmic and endosomal) recognize viral motifs, and most viruses have evolved evasion mechanisms.
evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C12-C15, C18-C19, C23-C24 represent established knowledge in viral immunology supported by general knowledge and appropriate citations. These provide necessary context for the study but are not novel findings. The claims are accurate representations of the field.

result: Prior work has identified alternative pathogen-sensing mechanisms involving pDC sensing of infected cells, including contact-dependent activation by DENV and other viruses. TLR7/9 signaling can show bifurcated patterns with differential IFN-I vs. NF-κB activation depending on subcellular compartmentalization.
evaluation: Claims C16-C22 and C25-C28 accurately cite prior literature establishing the foundation for the current study. The citations to Webster et al., 2016, Décembre et al., 2014, Swiecki and Colonna, 2015, and others are appropriate. These claims provide important context but represent prior work rather than new findings.

result: IRF5-dependent ISGs (Mx1, Ifit1) are upregulated in Irf3/7 DKO pDCs, and late ISG induction in Irf3/7 DKO mice is independent of pDC IRF7-mediated IFN-I, likely mediated by IRF1-induced type II IFN. Eventual DENV control in Irf3/7 DKO mice depends on the IFNγ response.
evaluation: Claims C49, C71-C72, C137-C139 document alternate IRF pathways with appropriate gene expression data and literature support. The late ISG induction (C71) and its independence from pDC-IRF7 signaling are demonstrated. The role of IRF1 (C72) and IFNγ in eventual control (C137-C138) are supported by citations. These findings contextualize the pDC-IRF7 response within broader antiviral immunity.

result: Prior literature establishes that neutrophils and monocytes modulate NK cell activation, pDCs are required for control of some but not all viral infections, and pDCs may serve as a failsafe upon systemic infection. NF-κB-dependent cytokines regulate IFNγ production by NK cells, and pDCs act with monocytes to potentiate NK cell responses.
evaluation: Claims C82, C112-C116, C145-C147 accurately cite relevant prior literature with appropriate references (Costa et al., 2017; Kang et al., 2008; Swiecki and Colonna, 2015; Schulthess et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2013; García-Sastre, 2017; Tomasello et al., 2014). These provide important context for interpreting the current findings but represent established knowledge.

result: The pDC:Irf7+ model offers unique opportunities to define pDC function and study cryptic pDC-mediated control of infections that might be masked by immune homeostasis when pDCs are depleted.
evaluation: Claims C117-C119 represent valid conclusions about the utility of the new mouse model. The model does provide advantages over depletion approaches (C116-C117), and the concept of masked pDC function (C119) is reasonable speculation. These are appropriate interpretive statements about the model's value.

result: Siglech expression by pDCs is inversely correlated with ISG upregulation in vivo, and NF-κB induction by DENV/CHIKV in other cell types likely requires cross-talk between IRF3 and NF-κB.
evaluation: Claims C122 and C128 provide supporting observations with appropriate data (C122: flow cytometry with citation to Puttur et al., 2013) and reasonable inference (C128: supported by citations to Freaney et al., 2013 and Iwanaszko and Kimmel, 2015). These are valid but secondary findings.

result: Speculative interpretations suggest that higher early DENV levels in pDC:Irf7+ mice may reflect immune cell recruitment, pDC responses may control systemic spread, differential IFNAR contributions between DENV and CHIKV may reflect virus-specific sensitivities, and segregating NF-κB and IRF7 responses may have therapeutic potential given the association of NF-κB cytokines with disease severity.
evaluation: Claims C62, C100, C104, C148-C149 represent speculative interpretations and potential applications. While these are reasonable hypotheses supported by citations (C62: Schmid and Harris, 2014; Seo et al., 2011; C100: Swiecki et al., 2013; C149: Chen et al., 2007; Dupuis-Maguiraga et al., 2012), they are not directly tested in the manuscript and require future validation.

result: IFNγ production by NK cells is restricted to the spleen (not blood), suggesting necessity for close apposition to infected/activated cells. pDC-IRF7 signaling is associated with neutrophil recruitment and monocyte activation in the spleen.
evaluation: Claims C143-C144 document tissue-specific immune responses with appropriate flow cytometry data. The inference about cell-cell proximity requirements (C143) is reasonable given the localized response. The association with neutrophil and monocyte responses (C144) is demonstrated, though causality is not definitively established.

result: Summary of key findings: DENV and CHIKV infected cells are sensed indirectly by pDCs, resulting in selective IRF7 activation and IFN-I production without inflammatory cytokines. A pDC-restricted IRF7 mouse model was developed, and despite undetectable IFN-I protein, pDC-IRF7 signaling controlled both viruses, protected from lethal CHIKV, and amplified downstream responses including accelerated NK cell-mediated type II IFN.
evaluation: Claims C4-C11 represent the abstract/summary statements that are supported by the comprehensive experimental data throughout the manuscript. These high-level conclusions accurately reflect the major findings documented in the detailed results. All key assertions are backed by appropriate experimental evidence.
